newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton settles lower and below key level.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton settles lower and below key level.

text.p: NYCE cotton closed weaker and under Friday's low as the speculators remained brisk and steady sellers, floor sources said.
Early trade selling pressured prices slightly below unchanged but the market moved sharply lower amid speculative selling once the benchmark December contract ran into sell stops around 75.10 cents.

The most-active month fell to the day's low of 74.70 cents, where trade buying stymied further losses. The failure to close over Friday's low of 75.33 cents, however, positions the market for further losses on Tuesday.
Light support in December was pegged at 74.00 cents followed by the contract low of 73.20 cents.
The December contract closed 0.58 cent weaker at 75.02 cents a lb, having ranged from 75.70 to 74.70 cents. The rest of the board closed 0.25 to 0.57 cent lower.
An estimated 9,000 lots changed hands on the day compared with Friday's official 8,122 lots.
The October/December spread closed at 0.05 cent compared with 0.15 cent on Friday.

Fundamentally, the market remains plagued by a dearth of news ahead of the U.S. Department of Agriculture's August supply and demand data. The report contains the first field survey-based estimates for the new crop.

The USDA will visit cotton fields in Texas, California, Mississippi, Arkansas and Louisiana to gauge the supply side of this years crop. Data for all other states will be based on subjective estimates.

Cotton in California and Arizona is progressing smoothly while crops in the Delta and Southeast are about three weeks behind schedule. The cotton has benefitted from the hot dry weather that has blanked the eastern part of the belt recently and could now use some rain.
The USDA will release its weekly progress report at 1600 EDT.
